newsitem.title: UK: Gold stays quietly above $346, palladium nervous.
newsitem.headline: Gold stays quietly above $346, palladium nervous.

text.p: The price of gold hovered aimlessly above $346 on Monday after a fund sell-off in New York that eroded most precious metals, dealers and analysts said.

Bullion fixed at $346.65 an ounce from $347.95 on Friday and compared with $346.95/$347.45 close. But it was above the nadir of $345.30 to which it was slashed by major trade houses and funds after worse-than-expected U.S. inflation figures.

"There is good physical demand for gold below $346. That's quite a key level," said one London dealer. "The market is very quiet. I suppose we are waiting for the Americans to try and show us the way."
The $346 area was an opportunity to buy after what he saw was a liquidation ahead of the weekend on lack of upside progress.
"I would expect gold to edge its way back to $348," said the dealer, although a decisive move to $350 was difficult for now.

Friday's U.S. producer price and retail sales data for March fuelled speculation about a fresh interest rate hike in May, wrecking Wall Street stocks. Higher interest rates also make gold look less attractive.
Some gold analysts thought the market was now vulnerable to a breach of key support at $345, which could prompt the funds to go short again.
"One has to be very careful if we test the lows of Friday," said a senior dealer in continental Europe.
"If we cannot hold $345.20, I expect stop loss orders and this could take the market to $341 and maybe test the lows of the year."
This week gold dealers will focus on the U.S. March consumer prices on Tuesday and industrial production on Wednesday for new clues on interest rates.
Palladium traded nervously at $154.25/$155.25, down $1.25, awaiting news on Russian sales to leading importer Japan. It had spiked above $160 last week but then slid back.
"I wouldn't be surprised to see a $5 move just depending on the next announcement that comes out of Russia," said a dealer.
A Russian finance ministry official said a decree that should allow exports from the world's biggest supplier to resume after a four-month delay would be signed this week.
But traders are sceptical that exports can resume soon.
Silver was five cents down on the day at $4.72/$4.74 and just off from Friday's lows, but analysts said a double bottom formation on charts at $4.70 could act as a magnet.
But there was also a possibility to test the $4.65 low on April 3. -- Clelia Oziel, London Newsroom +44-171-542 8071
